svg.title: Seasonal differencing vs deterministic seasonality
svg.desc: Treating seasonality as a stochastic component to be differenced away, or as a fixed pattern captured by dummies and Fourier terms.
svg.text: A stochastic component, or a fixed repeating pattern?
The same fixed pattern every year
Regression on dummies or Fourier terms
For stochastic seasonality, differencing is the right choice
Removing a fixed pattern leaves seasonality behind
A fixed seasonal cannot match a changing amplitude
Few parameters even for long periods
Changing amplitude calls for differencing; an identical yearly pattern calls for deterministic terms.
Mixing the two is common — difference first, then capture leftover calendar effects with dummies.
Decide with a seasonal unit root test, then confirm that no seasonality remains in the residuals.
Part 1 supplement · Connects to step 2 of the Box-Jenkins procedure (choosing d and D).
